correctness.rationale: From the explicitly defined dual norm N*(a,b)=max(|a|,|b|,|a+b|), the line-distance identity inf_lambda N(x+lambda y)=|det(x,y)|/N(y) holds. With x normalized to (1,t), 0<=t<=1, dihedral symmetry reduces y/N(y) to exactly three edges E0,E1,E2; E0 has no nontrivial isosceles solution, and remaining branch-active isosceles equalities force s+t<=3st or 1-2s-2t+3st>=0, respectively. Substitution q=sqrt((1-s)(1-t)) or sqrt(st), AM–GM yields q<=1/3 and determinant >=1-q²>=8/9. Equality in AM–GM and norm/isosc constraints forces r=||y||=1 and exactly the listed two symmetry-related chambers. Checked rational witness N(x±y)=4/3, determinant/N(y)=8/9. The argument is exhaustive because the hexagon edges partition the direction circle.
residual_risks: Finite planar exact chamber proof; need interpret dihedral isometries of the affine hexagon, not arbitrary Euclidean rotations.
